q: Between the plates of a velocity selector the electric field strength is $3.0 \cdot 10^{4}\,\text{V/m}$ and the magnetic flux density $0.10\,\text{T}$. At what speed do ions pass straight through the selector?
a: $v = \tfrac{E}{B} = \tfrac{3.0 \cdot 10^{4}\,\text{V/m}}{0.10\,\text{T}} = 3.0 \cdot 10^{5}\,\text{m/s}$, whatever the mass or charge of the ion.

q: A proton and an electron fly at the same speed perpendicular to the same magnetic field. How do their paths differ?
a: The paths curve in opposite directions, because the charges have opposite signs. The magnitudes of the charges are equal, so the radius $r = mv : (|q|B)$ is proportional to the mass: the path of the electron is about $1840$ times smaller than that of the proton.
